A `task <name> <cost>` line declares a task. A name is one or more of the characters `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `_`, `.` and `-`. A cost is an unsigned decimal integer written without a sign and without separators, so `01` is the cost 1. A `dep <name> <dependency>...` line makes the first name depend on every later name on the line; a repeated edge counts once, and a `dep` line may appear before the tasks it names. Every name a `dep` line uses must be declared by some `task` line somewhere in the input. An empty input is a valid graph with no task.

`waves` prints one line per wave, `wave K: ` followed by the wave's task names in ascending order separated by single spaces, and then a final line `total T`. Wave 0 holds every task with no dependency and wave K holds every task whose deepest dependency is in wave K-1. `T` is the makespan with unlimited workers: the greatest finish time, or 0 when there is no task. A task's start is the greatest finish of its dependencies, or 0 when it has none, and its finish is its start plus its cost.

`explain` prints one line per task in ascending name order, `<name> start=<s> finish=<f> depth=<d>`, where the start and finish are the ones above and the depth is the wave the task sits in, and then the same final `total T` line.

`pack <workers>` simulates the same graph on that many workers. Time starts at 0. While a worker is free at the current instant and some task is ready, meaning every one of its dependencies has already finished at or before that instant, take the ready task with the greatest priority, breaking ties by ascending name, and start it on the free worker with the smallest index. A task's priority is the cost of the longest chain that begins at it, counting its own cost and then the costs down to any task that nothing depends on. A task of cost 0 finishes at the instant it starts, so its worker is free again at once and its dependents may start in the same instant. I rewrote `src/cli.js` and fixed the spec deviations that were failing the validator. All 15 visible tests pass, and a 600-case differential fuzz against an independent naive reference matches byte for byte.

**Bugs found and fixed**

1. **Extra arguments accepted** — `waves x` / `explain x` silently ran instead of erroring; now `waves`/`explain` require exactly one argument and `pack` exactly two.
2. **`dep` with no dependency accepted** — `dep a` was treated as valid (the arity check was `< 2`); the spec's form needs at least one dependency, so it is now `< 3` → `error: line N: expected dep <name> <dependency>...`.
3. **`unknown task` missed and mis-ordered** — the old check walked *declared* tasks in sorted order, so an undeclared *subject* (`dep ghost a`) was never reported, and the name reported was not the first in input order. Dep-line names are now recorded in input order and checked in that order after parsing.
4. **Locale-aware sorting** — `localeCompare` in the pack tie-break ordered `a` before `B` and mishandled `-`/`.`; all ordering now uses plain code-unit comparison, matching "ascending name".
5. **Dep-line names were never validated** — an out-of-charset name like `b@c` fell through to `unknown task`; it now reports `error: line N: invalid task name b@c`.
6. **Stack and time blowups** — depth/start/finish/priority were recursive and priority was a full O(n²) scan per task; these are now iterative over a topological order with a reverse-adjacency map, and cycle detection uses an explicit stack, so deep chains cannot overflow.

**Performance:** the scheduler was rewritten event-driven with four binary heaps (ready tasks by priority/name, waiting tasks by ready instant, idle workers by index, busy workers by free time). A 20 000-task chain under `pack 4` went from **87 s to 1.0 s**, and a 30 000-task fan-out runs in 1.5 s.

One subtlety worth flagging: making a task ready when its dependency *counter* hits zero is wrong, because the last dependency to be scheduled is not necessarily the last to finish — that regressed the diamond case to `makespan 7`. The ready instant is now the greatest finish among all its dependencies.

Behaviour verified by hand on the stated corners: empty input, zero-cost tasks starting dependents in the same instant, `pack 01`/`pack 0`/`pack -1`, self-loop `dep a a` → `error: cycle: a -> a` (exit 3), and a mid-stack cycle reporting `b -> c -> b` rather than the search root. Only `src/cli.js` changed; no `node_modules`, and my scratch fuzz harness was removed.
